name: Seattle
industries: Cloud technology and e-commerce dominate, with aerospace heritage and healthcare systems adding classical program demand.
intro:
Seattle's two hometown giants shaped how the world builds software and ships packages, and the city's project culture carries both DNAs: cloud-scale agile delivery at Amazon, Microsoft and their orbit of partners, plus aerospace program management traditions from a century of Boeing. Scrum credentials are near-universal in the tech corridor from South Lake Union to Redmond; PMP anchors aerospace, healthcare and the enterprise side. Live online batches run year-round with sensible Seattle timings — a full Saturday–Sunday weekend cohort plus a midweek Wednesday–Thursday option — so you train during comfortable local daytime hours; the schedule table below lists every upcoming date with its exact Seattle start and finish. The format stays: live weekend instruction, exam application support, mocks, and trainer access until you pass.

Seattle's delivery culture was shaped by cloud-scale engineering: the tech giants and the ecosystem around them run programs measured in fleets and regions, while aerospace and healthcare add classical program governance south and north of the city. Certified project leadership reads credibly across both — and stands out in tech resumes precisely because engineers often skip it. The course runs live online over two consecutive days shown in Seattle local time on this page. Puget Sound compensation for certified project roles competes with the Bay at lower cost; the sourced Seattle entries below give named, dated figures. The employer list shows the cloud-aerospace-healthcare mix, and vendor organizations serving the giants can certify delivery teams via private cohorts.
